subject: economics
title: The Short-Run Phillips Curve
welcome_lead: A trade-off between unemployment and inflation - in the short run.
meta_desc: A-Level Phillips Curve: original short-run trade-off.
final_note: Short-run trade-off works only when expectations are stuck.

concepts.def: 1958 - UK data showed a stable inverse relationship.
Period before wage and price expectations adjust.
Accepting more inflation for less unemployment.
Wages slow to adjust to inflation expectations.

walkthroughs.body_html: A.W. Phillips analysed UK wage and unemployment data from 1861 to 1957 and found an inverse relationship - high inflation went with low unemployment.
When AD rises, firms hire more workers (cutting unemployment) and raise prices (creating inflation). With sticky wages, real wages fall and labour demand jumps.
1960s policymakers tried to pick a point on the curve - accepting more inflation to push unemployment down. The 1970s would show this strategy collapsing.
